class.name: VGAMasterNode
class.brief_description: Root node for the Visual Godot Agents plugin. Place one in your main scene.
class.description: Runs [member num_envs] parallel instances of [member environment_scene] in separate SubViewports, and synchronizes observations and actions with a Python training process via POSIX shared memory and semaphores. The shared memory region and semaphores are identified by [member ipc_name]. On [method Node._ready], the node initializes the environments and the IPC transport, and quits the application if initialization fails. Each physics step, [method Node._physics_process] automatically writes observations into shared memory, signals Python, blocks until Python responds with actions, and dispatches those actions to each environment's [VGAAgentNode]. Your environment scene must contain exactly one [VGAAgentNode] subclass. The Python process must create the semaphores and open the shared memory region using the same [member ipc_name] before Godot starts.

method.name: get_user_args

members.member: The scene representing one environment instance. Must contain exactly one [VGAAgentNode] subclass. One instance is created per parallel environment.
Number of parallel environment instances to run.
Width and height of the visual observation rendered by each SubViewport. Determines the size of the visual observation block in shared memory.

Identifier used to name the POSIX shared memory region ([code]/[ipc_name][/code]) and semaphores ([code]/[ipc_name]_env_ready[/code], [code]/[ipc_name]_act_ready[/code]). Must match the name used on the Python side.

Physics tick rate in Hz. The fixed time delta visible to agent logic and to Python's [code]env.step()[/code] is [code]1 / step_rate_hz[/code]. Named in Hz to match RL convention. All environment logic must use [method Node._physics_process] (or physics-mode equivalents such as physics-mode [Timer] nodes) — [method Node._process] receives a wall-clock delta scaled by [code]time_scale[/code] and is not suitable for simulation logic.
